changedFields.before: Step 4: Evaluate Alternatives and Set Criteria. Based on the evidence, Aisha saw that a new packing machine would only address 30% of the delays. She brainstormed alternatives: (1) improve supplier communication, (2) implement address verification software, (3) hire temporary packing staff, (4) do nothing. Her criteria were cost, speed of implementation, and impact on customer satisfaction.
changedFields.after: Step4: Evaluate Alternatives and Set Criteria. In the ten observed delayed orders,3/10 were classified as packing backlog and7/10 as supplier or address issues. These are cause shares in this small sample, not a forecast that a machine fixes all three packing cases or two other changes remove all seven. Compare supplier communication, address checks, temporary packing staff, a machine and doing nothing against cost, implementation time and customer impact.

changedFields.before: Step 5: Implement a Bounded Trial. Aisha decided to first focus on supplier communication and address verification, as these addressed 70% of the issues. She implemented a new supplier check-in process for two weeks and integrated a free address verification tool. Her stop condition was if late deliveries due to these two causes did not decrease by 50% within a month, she would re-evaluate and consider other options like temporary staff or a new machine.
changedFields.after: Step5: Implement a Bounded Trial. Try supplier communication and address checking on a limited scale and measure new delay counts and rates with a consistent denominator and period. Retain the proposed review condition: if delays attributed to those causes do not decrease by50% within a month, re-evaluate the options. This is a test target, not an achieved result; neither the ten-case cause distribution nor the solutions' effectiveness is guaranteed to generalize.
